# ECN-2026-037 - Change notice - Machining radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-RR01

Reason for change
- Background: During a routine review of machining and securing procedures for the mandrel assembly on Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01), maintenance and reliability teams identified variability in clamp preload and evidence of recurring fastener loosening after heavy machining cycles. Root cause analysis traced the issue to a discrepancy between previously applied clamp bolt torque and the clamping requirement needed to maintain mandrel positional stability under radial load and vibration.
- Objective: Standardize the mandrel clamp bolt tightening requirement and update controlled procedures and records to eliminate preload variability, reduce unplanned downtime, and improve part quality and dimensional consistency coming out of EQ-P2-L3-RR01.
- Rationale: A single, specified clamp bolt torque value provides a repeatable preload target, reduces operator interpretation during maintenance, and aligns mechanical joint behavior with design intent. The chosen value balances joint clamp force with bolt yield and joint surface conditions, minimizing risk of fatigue or joint slip while maintaining maintainability.

Affected items
- Equipment: All mandrel clamp assemblies on Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01) are affected. This includes the clamp bolts and their associated washers and threaded interfaces as assembled on the mandrel housing.
- Procedures: Existing standard operating procedures that reference mandrel clamp bolt tightening for P2 line radial ring rolling mill machining are affected. See SOP-P2-L3-01, SOP-P2-L3-02, and SOP-P2-L3-04 for related process steps and safety precautions that will be updated to reflect the new torque specification.
- Training and skill checks: Operator and maintenance qualifications that verify correct torque application on this mill will be modified to include demonstration to the new requirement.
- Records and logs: Preventive maintenance records, torque calibration records, and post-maintenance inspection checklists that capture mandrel clamp bolt torque will be updated to record the specified value.

Implementation
- New specification: The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01) is 470 N·m. This value is to be applied every time the mandrel clamp bolts are installed or re-torqued following disassembly or adjustment.
- Tools and calibration: Use calibrated torque wrenches and, where applicable, calibrated torque multipliers that are within their calibration cycle and traceable to the calibration laboratory. Operators must confirm the calibration sticker or record prior to applying torque. If a torque tool is out of calibration, do not proceed until a compliant tool is provided.
- Application method: Tighten clamp bolts in a controlled, incremental sequence to final torque, observing the manufacturer guidance for even seating of the clamp. After achieving specified torque, perform a verification pass to confirm torque retention. If any bolt does not retain torque, disassemble, inspect the bolt, washer, and threaded interface for damage or contamination, clean and reassemble, and reapply torque.
- Verification and inspection: Post-torque visual inspection of clamp seating and a functional run check of the mandrel assembly should be performed. If abnormal noise, movement, or vibration is observed, stop operation and perform a detailed inspection before resuming machining.
- Procedure updates: Revise SOP-P2-L3-01, SOP-P2-L3-02, and SOP-P2-L3-04 to incorporate the new torque value, the required tooling and calibration verification steps, the tightening sequence, the recheck methodology, and the criteria for nonconformance. Each updated SOP must include the exact torque value as shown above and cross-reference this ECN.
- Training: Implement a training brief for affected maintenance and operations staff. Training will cover the reason for the change, the new torque value, correct use of torque tools, and the updated verification steps. Successful completion must be documented in the training record system referenced by plant practice.
- Example scenarios: Provide technicians with realistic examples in the updated SOPs showing how to proceed if a bolt does not hold torque, including steps for inspection, cleaning, replacement of damaged components, and escalation to engineering when thread damage is found that affects clamping integrity.

Records to keep
- Torque application record: For each mandrel clamp bolt operation on EQ-P2-L3-RR01, record the applied torque value, the tool identification and calibration status, the name of the technician, and a statement confirming verification pass. Store this record in the machine maintenance folder and in the electronic maintenance system as required by plant policy.
- Calibration records: Maintain current calibration certificates for all torque tools used on this procedure. Link calibration records to the torque application record.
- Post-maintenance inspection: Keep inspection checklists and any vibration or run data collected after reassembly. If follow-up corrective action was required, attach the corrective action record and root cause notes.
- Training evidence: Document attendance and competency check results for all personnel trained on the new requirement. Include signed or electronically approved training completion evidence.
- SOP revision control: Keep a copy of the updated SOP-P2-L3-01, SOP-P2-L3-02, and SOP-P2-L3-04 showing revision history and the ECN reference.

Approvals
- Engineering approval: Process engineering must review the change for mechanical integrity implications and accept the specified mandrel clamp bolt torque for EQ-P2-L3-RR01. The engineering review shall include verification that the torque value is compatible with the clamp and bolt specifications on the mill.
- Maintenance approval: Maintenance management is responsible for confirming that tooling, spare parts, and calibration support are in place prior to implementation.
- Operations approval: Line operations management must confirm that the implementation plan is compatible with production scheduling and that trained operators will be available for any planned rework or verification runs.
- Document control: Update the configuration of SOP-P2-L3-01, SOP-P2-L3-02, and SOP-P2-L3-04 to reference this ECN and the mandated torque value. Ensure controlled copies are issued and superseded copies are archived.

Disposition and follow-up
- Implement the change after all approvals are recorded and required resources are in place. Monitor the first production runs after implementation for evidence of improved clamp stability and reduced rework or downtime. Capture lessons learned and feed them into continuous improvement channels.
- Reference SOP-P2-L3-01, SOP-P2-L3-02, and SOP-P2-L3-04 for procedural context and for any safety steps that accompany clamp handling and torque application.
